## Current collaboration contract (effective 2026-09-15)

The detailed state and execution strategy are maintained in
`docs/research/PROJECT_HANDOFF.md`. The working loop is deliberative:
Claude Code is the primary strategy author and implementation owner; Codex is an
independent, adversarial reviewer. Claude Code proposes a falsifiable hypothesis,
actual parent, exact change, validation protocol, budget, artifacts, risks, and
rollback/stop rule. Codex checks those claims against source, tests, leakage,
graph semantics, numerical behavior, reproducibility, and budget, and may require
revision. The proposal may be implemented or executed only after a versioned
record contains the proposal, critique, revisions, and explicit `CONSENSUS`.
`NO_CONSENSUS` is a stop condition that is returned to the user for direction.

Claude Code may lead implementation after consensus, but implementation does not
replace review: Codex must independently inspect the diff and run proportionate
validation. Future experiments must set
`admission.require_codex_review: true` (and may set
`reviewer_provider: codex`), request review with
`scripts/request_codex_review.py`, and require a fresh experiment-specific Codex
`PASS` before execution. Legacy experiment configs and receipts, including
exp_055, remain Claude-based and are preserved without retroactive rewriting.
After execution, Codex audits raw artifacts and metrics before Claude interprets
the result and proposes the next strategy. Historical records are immutable
evidence and must not be silently rewritten.

The project is in a late-stage accuracy push. With explicit user authorization,
high-risk/high-reward experiments are encouraged, including potentially
framework-changing detector, association, decoding, or joint-lineage designs.
Such experiments may fail and should be selected for credible upside and
information value. They must nevertheless retain exact provenance, a reversible
snapshot, bounded resources, an explicit stop rule, leakage protection,
independent graph/metric audits, and honest separation of local proxy evidence
from Public LB evidence. Aggressive research expands the search space; it does
not weaken validation, budget, tracking, model-allowance, leaderboard, or
promotion gates. Any major direction change remains subject to user approval.

## Codex

Role: independent principal reviewer and research partner. Codex may implement
changes after the Claude Code proposal has reached explicit consensus, but must
challenge the proposal independently and audit the resulting implementation.

Codex may modify project code, create experiment configs, run local tests, invoke controller
scripts, launch approved Kaggle experiments, inspect outputs, and update experiment records.

Codex must not delete datasets or experiment history, expose credentials, silently change the
validation protocol, bypass experiment tracking, exceed the GPU/submission budget, or push to an
important remote branch without user approval.

Kaggle leaderboard submissions are capped at three per America/New_York calendar day. Before every
submission, Codex must query the remote submission history, confirm the candidate is a meaningful
milestone rather than a duplicate probe, and record the result in `SUBMISSION_BUDGET.json`.

All newly created or revised notebooks, experiment configs, continuation notes, and technical
documentation must use English only. Imported third-party source may retain its original language
only inside an immutable provenance archive; any active working copy must use English.

Publish a cleaned milestone notebook under `src/` when the project reaches a substantial, completed
research milestone, such as a frozen validation baseline, a confirmed method improvement, a promoted
baseline, or a fully reproducible release candidate. Do not publish routine fixes, failed attempts,
or experiments that have not produced a stable conclusion. Milestone notebooks must use a monotonic
`biohub_vNN_<short_name>.ipynb` name, contain an English provenance/summary cell, have no saved error
outputs, and be listed in `src/MILESTONES.md`. Never overwrite an existing milestone version.

Codex and Claude Code must each retain at least 10 percent of the user's weekly allowance. When
either visible remaining allowance reaches 10 percent, stop new model calls, save the current
notebook/config/experiment state and a concise continuation note, and wait for an explicit user
request to continue. If exact allowance is unavailable, avoid repeated or open-ended model calls
and surface that uncertainty before starting another substantial review.

Before every Kaggle remote launch, Codex must ensure the experiment has one explicit hypothesis, an
exact change description, a parent, a smoke-test pass, sufficient budget, and a fresh,
experiment-specific Codex review recorded as `PASS`. New experiment configs must set
`admission.require_codex_review: true` (optionally `reviewer_provider: codex`) and use
`scripts/request_codex_review.py`; a missing review or a `REVISE`/`BLOCK` result prohibits
launch. Historical Claude-based configs and receipts remain valid historical evidence.
Public leaderboard results are secondary evidence.

At the start of a resumed research session, Codex must read `GOAL.md` and
`.private/current/CONTINUATION.md`, then inspect the active experiment record before creating,
rebuilding, collecting, or launching an experiment.

## Claude Code

Role: primary research strategist and implementation owner. For agreed work,
Claude Code's default mode includes authoring and editing. Claude switches to
read-only inspection only while acting in an explicit review or audit role; the
review output is captured in the experiment directory and mirrored to
`CLAUDE_REVIEW.md`.

Claude must not edit training or controller code during a review.
Claude reviews should be narrowly scoped and must not be retried automatically after a timeout or
quota stop.

At the start of a resumed review session, Claude must treat `GOAL.md` and
`.private/current/CONTINUATION.md` as the current handoff. Older historical material in
`CLAUDE.md` must not override a newer dated checkpoint.

## Experiment Controller

Role: deterministic execution, state, budget, and recovery layer.

The controller validates and executes experiments. It must never invent hypotheses, weaken an
admission gate, infer a metric from arbitrary prose, print credentials, or promote a baseline
without an explicit promotion request.

## User

Role: research director. User approval is required for credential changes, unusually large GPU
spend, leaderboard submission bursts, restricted/private data, destructive operations, and major
research-direction changes.
